scripts.title: Santa wore red in 1821
scripts.headline: SANTA WORE RED IN 1821
scripts.text: Many people believe Coca-Cola made Santa red in the nineteen thirties. But look at The Children's Friend, a little book printed in New York in eighteen twenty-one. In one surviving copy, now at Yale University, Santeclaus is already wearing a red coat.

scripts.title: Santa once wore the flag
scripts.headline: SANTA ONCE WORE THE FLAG
scripts.text: In January eighteen sixty-three, during the American Civil War, Thomas Nast drew Santa Claus for Harper's Weekly. His Santa visited a Union army camp, in a coat of stars and striped trousers. It was printed in black and white.

scripts.title: In 1821, Santa had one reindeer
scripts.headline: IN 1821, SANTA HAD ONE REINDEER
scripts.text: In eighteen twelve, Washington Irving pictured Saint Nicholas riding over the tops of the trees in a wagon. In eighteen twenty-one, a little book showed his sleigh pulled by a single reindeer. Two years later, a poem gave him eight tiny reindeer.
